what: Q1:43 says a seller adds a place to sell to on WooCommerce by 'a country added to the shipped setting "Selling location(s)"', but that setting is a select with 'default' => 'all' whose options are 'Sell to all countries', 'Sell to all countries, except for...' and 'Sell to specific countries'; its desc is 'This option lets you limit which countries you are willing to sell to.' Countries are listed in the separate settings 'Sell to specific countries' (woocommerce_specific_allowed_countries) or 'Sell to all countries, except for...', so by default every country is already sold to and the point leaves that out. Q1:11 and Q1:62 hold.
fix: Q1:43: 'on WooCommerce, the shipped setting "Selling location(s)", which by default is "Sell to all countries" and "lets you limit which countries you are willing to sell to", with a country added under "Sell to specific countries"'.

what: Unsure: Q1:14 'BigCommerce and WooCommerce set rates by geography, in zones "based on country, state, or postal code" and, in WooCommerce's shipped code, by a rate's "2 digit country code"' can be read as WooCommerce also setting tax rates in zones; WooCommerce's source is a tax rates table whose columns are 'Country code', 'State code' and 'Postcode / ZIP', each rate a row ('A 2 digit country code, e.g. US. fix: Q1:14: 'BigCommerce sets rates in zones "based on country, state, or postal code"; WooCommerce's shipped code sets each tax rate by a "2 digit country code" (with a state code and postcode)'.

what: The source is the shipping zones page's 'Rest of the world' row: 'An optional zone you can use to set the shipping method(s) available to any regions that have not been listed above', i.e. regions in no other shipping zone. Q1:19 drops 'to set the shipping method(s) available to' and presents it as WooCommerce's treatment of buyers outside the store's places, and Q1:74 says WooCommerce makes buying by a buyer in no market 'optional'; the source speaks of shipping methods for unlisted regions, not of whether such buyers may buy (which countries are sold to is the separate setting 'Selling location(s)').
fix: Q1:19: 'WooCommerce's shipped code has "An optional zone you can use to set the shipping method(s) available to any regions that have not been listed above"'. Q1:74: drop WooCommerce from 'make it optional', or say 'WooCommerce has an optional shipping zone for regions not listed in other zones'.

what: The record's scope and Q1:39 say 'store country YE'. The cited file says only 'Each entry is keyed by the two-letter country code'; the country it is looked up with is the Payments settings' business location: Payments::get_country() returns 'The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to use for the overall business location. If the user didn't set a location, the WC base location country code is used.' (the user's 'business_country_code', recorded as 'business_location_update'), passed to get_extension_suggestions( $location ). So YE is the business location, which is the store's base country only where the user set none. That the YE list holds only VISA (Q1:39 'suggests only VISA') holds: get_country_extensions processes only $this->country_extensions[ $country_code ].
fix: Record scope: 'business location country YE (the store base country where the user set no business location)'. Q1:39: 'WooCommerce's code (shipped) suggests only VISA where the business location is YE'.

what: The source limits it to WooPayments: under 'Other countries' on 'WooPayments in Your Country Documentation', 'the WooCommerce team is actively working to make WooPayments available to other countries.
